To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

adsorption of polymer from solutions of polymeric mixtures in the transition concentration range is a complex process and the adsorption is characterized by the existence of two mechanisms: adsorption of individual chains and adsorption of aggregates of macromolecules.
adsorption of polymer from dilute solutions is governed by the conformation of adsorbed polymer chains and that the adsorption layer structure changes with temperature and concentration.
the effect of temperature on the adsorption of polymethacrylates and polystyrenes from their binary and multicomponent solutions is different depending on the solution regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of temperature on the adsorption of polymethacrylate and polystyrenes and their mixtures in the transition region between dilute and semidilute concentration regimes.
the study of the adsorption of polymethacrylates from solutions of various concentration regimes and temperatures.
the effect of temperature on the adsorption of polymethylmethacrylate, polybutylmethacrylate and their mixtures on silica.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

adsorption of macropolymer from dilute solutions is a process of adsorption of single chains, whereas adsorption from semidilute and concentrated solutions is a process which includes the adsorption of macroglobules and macropolymer aggregates.

the adsorption of polymolecular layers of polymers from solutions of different concentration regimes at various temperatures is characterized by a change in adsorption mechanism and by the change of the adsorption parameters, such as adsorption layer thickness, fraction of bound segments, and preferential adsorption.

the effect of temperature on the adsorption from the solutions of polymers and their mixtures in the transition region of dilute to semilute solutions is determined by the competition between two mechanisms of the adsorption: the adsorption of single macromolecules and adsorption of the macromolecular aggregates, and the effect of temperature is governed by the relative contribution of these mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effect of temperature on polymer adsorption from dilute and semidilute regimes is determined by the competition of two factors: the temperature dependence of the segment-surface interaction energy and the temperature dependence of polymer solution viscosity.
the adsorption of polymethylmethacrylate and polystyrenes from their mixtures is determined by the competition of the two polymers for adsorption sites at the surface.
adsorption isotherm and the fraction of bound segment for PBMA in the transition region are similar to the adsorption from binary solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adsorption layer structure is determined not only by the concentration of the solution from which the adsorption occurs, but also by the temperature at which the adsorption process takes place.
adsorption of macroparticles in semidilute region is characterized by the formation of adsorption layers with a thickness which is much larger than the size of the adsorbing macroparticle.
the adsorption layer of the polymer in the transition region is characterized by the presence in it of both macromolecular aggregates and single macromolecules.
